security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel context switch, KVM vCPU switch, signal delivery (sigreturn), or ptrace (PTRACE_SETREGSET) fails to save/restore sstatus.CRGE, causing a process or VM to observe CRGE enable/disable state from a different security context, or the kernel sets CRGE=1 without zero-initializing PTE.CD and PTE.CRG bits in all user page tables, causing hardware to trigger unexpected store exceptions or silently set PTE.CD via Svadu hardware dirty tracking on pages whose PTE was configured under the pre-Svucrg PTE.CRW-only semantics.
security_spec.summary: sstatus.CRGE is a new per-context opt-in bit that toggles PTE.CRW/CD/CRG into a 3-bit capability-access field; if the kernel does not save/restore it on context switch or fails to virtualize vsstatus.CRGE in KVM, the hardware will reinterpret the same PTE bits under different semantics per thread, causing silent PTE.CD dirty-tracking corruption (Svadu) or spurious capability-store traps (Svade) on pages created by CRGE-unaware code.

findings.finding: Context switch saves full sstatus into thread.sum (line 442-443), but on restore masks to SR_SUM only (line 450: 'and s0, s0, s1') and uses csrs (set-bits only, line 451) rather than csrw. This means: (a) any CRGE/UCRG bit stored in the saved value is discarded by the AND mask, and (b) csrs only sets bits without clearing, so a previous task's CRGE=1 state leaks into the next task. A task expecting CRGE=0 would run with CRGE=1, causing hardware to interpret PTE.CD/CRG bits under Svucrg semantics on page tables configured under pre-Svucrg PTE.CRW-only semantics.
findings.snippet:
csrr  s0, CSR_STATUS
REG_S s0, TASK_THREAD_SUM_RA(a3)
...
REG_L s0,  TASK_THREAD_SUM_RA(a4)
li    s1,  SR_SUM
and   s0,  s0, s1
csrs  CSR_STATUS, s0

findings.finding: thread_struct has only 'unsigned long sum' (line 114) to store the SUM bit from sstatus. There is no field to persist the full sstatus value across context switches. If CRGE/UCRG is added to sstatus, thread_struct must gain a dedicated field (or repurpose 'sum' to hold the full sstatus word), otherwise the hardware CRGE state is lost on every context switch.

restore_sigcontext copies only sizeof(sc->sc_regs) == sizeof(struct user_regs_struct) from the signal frame into pt_regs. user_regs_struct contains 31 GPRs plus pc but does NOT include sstatus (it is the 32nd field in pt_regs, after t6). Therefore sigreturn does not restore sstatus.CRGE. After signal delivery, the process runs with whatever hardware sstatus.CRGE value the kernel left behind, potentially observing CRGE state from before the signal or from a different context.

setup_sigcontext copies only sizeof(sc->sc_regs) GPRs (via user_regs_struct) to the signal frame, excluding pt_regs->status/sstatus. The process's CRGE state is not preserved in the signal frame. If the signal handler modifies CRGE (or the kernel changes it during signal delivery), the original CRGE value is irrecoverably lost on sigreturn.

riscv_gpr_get exposes only sizeof(struct user_regs_struct) to ptrace, which excludes sstatus. A debugger or checkpoint/restore tool (CRIU) cannot read sstatus.CRGE via PTRACE_GETREGSET. Full user-visible register state is incomplete for Svucrg-aware processes.

riscv_gpr_set uses user_regset_copyin limited to sizeof(struct user_regs_struct), so PTRACE_SETREGSET cannot restore sstatus.CRGE. Checkpoint/restore of a process with CRGE=1 would silently restore it with CRGE=0 (or whatever the kernel's current hardware sstatus holds).

user_regs_struct defines 31 GPRs (pc through t6) but omits sstatus. This is the UAPI structure used by signal frames, ptrace, and core dumps. The struct comment (line 21) states it 'must form a prefix of struct pt_regs', but pt_regs->status sits after t6 at offset 32*sizeof(long). Adding sstatus to user_regs_struct would break UAPI, so an extension-header mechanism (like the existing RISCV_V_MAGIC/RISCV_ZICFISS_MAGIC chain) is needed for CRGE.

KVM guest entry uses csrrw (atomic read-write swap) for CSR_SSTATUS (line 48), preserving all sstatus bits including any future CRGE/UCRG. The full-width exchange correctly isolates host and guest sstatus, including Svucrg state.
findings.snippet:
REG_L t0, (KVM_ARCH_GUEST_SSTATUS)(a0)
csrrw t0, CSR_SSTATUS, t0
...
REG_S t0, (KVM_ARCH_HOST_SSTATUS)(a0)

findings.finding: KVM guest exit uses csrrw for CSR_SSTATUS (line 155), atomically saving guest sstatus and restoring host sstatus. Guest CRGE/UCRG bits are correctly preserved in the guest context structure across VCPU switches.
findings.snippet:
REG_L t2, (KVM_ARCH_HOST_SSTATUS)(a0)
csrrw t2, CSR_SSTATUS, t2
REG_S t2, (KVM_ARCH_GUEST_SSTATUS)(a0)

findings.finding: VCPU context reset initializes sstatus to SR_SPP|SR_SPIE (line 72), which implicitly sets CRGE=0 and UCRG=0 since these bits are currently undefined (zero). This is a safe default. The full-width csr_write/csr_read operations in kvm_arch_vcpu_load (line 605) and kvm_arch_vcpu_put (line 673) correctly preserve all bits of VSSTATUS including future CRGE.

Trap redirect modifies VSSTATUS using read-modify-write with bitwise AND/OR on SPP, SPIE, and SIE only (lines 145, 150, 155). The ncsr_read/ncsr_write are full-width operations, so any future CRGE/UCRG bits in VSSTATUS are preserved across trap redirection.
